A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FCP research work, with matching title and authors. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original AR/VAR simulations and wind, traffic and solar evaluations in Tables 1–2, plus additional simulation results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 reports original real-world evaluations using two base predictors, encoder and vector-field ablations, and additional coverage analyses in Section 5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: v1 trains a Transformer-conditioned continuous flow. v2 introduces classifier-free guidance, random null conditioning during training, and guided/unguided vector-field combination during inference (Equations 12–13 and Algorithm 1). The stated encoder input also changes from feature history in v1 Equation 6 to concatenated feature and residual history.

E1.justification: v2 removes both synthetic test families: independent autoregressive sequences and vector autoregressive sequences from v1 Section 5.2 and its appendices. Wind, traffic and solar remain, with the same outcome-dimension coverage. The removal substantially reduces controlled synthetic coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds OT-CP by Thurin et al. and CONTRA by Fang et al. to the real-world comparisons in Table 1; v1 only cited CONTRA. All seven original baselines remain in the corresponding 0.95-coverage comparison. These additions substantially extend comparisons to alternative transport and flow methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds LSTM predictors trained on the first half of each sequence, followed by an 80/10/10 split of the remaining evaluation sequence. It revises validation use and baseline calibration allocation, adds 0.90-target real-world evaluations, and changes several hyperparameters. Volume estimation switches to Sobol sampling with 4096/8192/16384 samples instead of v1's Monte Carlo counts of 1000/5000/10000.

E4.justification: v2 adds encoder-removal ablations, MLP-versus-iResNet comparisons examining the bi-Lipschitz assumption, rolling coverage with 20-point windows, and real-world confidence-level sensitivity experiments. v1's paired region-size stability plots and TFT/DeepAR target-inflation simulations are removed. These changes substantially revise the questions tested and supporting analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark means and standard deviations over five independent experiments. v2 newly specifies a relative-standard-error threshold below 0.01 for selecting volume-estimation sample counts; v1 only reports that larger counts had little effect. No increase in experimental repeat counts is documented.

E6.justification: Many retained-dataset results change. For wind with two outcomes and the LOO bootstrap predictor, FCP's reported coverage/size changes from 0.953/1.16 in v1 Table 2 to 0.951/0.88 in v2 Table 1. Method and protocol revisions prevent interpreting this as a same-setting gain. New predictor, baseline, ablation, confidence-level and timing results are added, while simulation results disappear.

T1.justification: v2 adds finite-sample conditional-coverage bounds for i.i.d. and stationary strongly mixing scores, explicit regularity and prediction-error assumptions, and extensive supporting proofs in Appendix A. Existing probability-mass preservation and Jacobian arguments are retained and reformulated. v1's computational-complexity bound is removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion newly foreground classifier-free guidance and claim finite-sample conditional-coverage guarantees, beyond v1's marginal-coverage contribution. The smaller-prediction-set claim remains, but its stated empirical support changes from simulated and real-world datasets to real-world datasets alone.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies coverage by learned-flow accuracy and interprets conditional guarantees through predictor accuracy and score-dependence assumptions, extending v1's simpler mass-preservation explanation. It also introduces guidance-scale tuning advice and explanations connecting baseline performance to temporal or local correlations and possible applicability beyond exchangeability.

D1.justification: v2 adds null-conditioning probabilities, guidance scales, Softplus activation, detailed baseline calibration and CONTRA implementation settings, hardware specifications and timing tables. Hyperparameter documentation is substantially revised. Conversely, v1's explicit standardization description disappears. Both versions identify the same code repository.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning to optimal-transport and rank methods by Klein and Thurin, minimum-volume and template approaches by Braun and Tumu, and classifier-free guidance literature. Portions of v1's functional-data and probabilistic-forecasting discussion disappear. The anonymous CONTRA reference and Fang et al. refer to the same work; that attribution update alone is not a new citation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, problem setup, method exposition and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The separate Related Works section is absorbed into the introduction, theory becomes a standalone section, and the appendices are reorganized around proofs, experimental settings, datasets and additional analyses.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figures 1–2, removes v1's covered/uncovered transformation figure and paired region-size plots, and adds rolling-coverage Figure 3. The main comparison table is rebuilt with base-predictor groups and additional methods. New ablation, timing and confidence-level tables, together with Algorithm 1, substantially change the display structure.

improvement.justification: v2 adds valuable baselines, LSTM evaluations, ablations and implementation details, but removes v1's controlled simulations. Its new conditional guarantee has unresolved proof mismatches: Equation 110 substitutes empirical-quantile sets for Equation 14's Gaussian-radius rule, and Equation 99 uses squared norms for scores defined as norms in Section 4.2. These concerns affect a new headline contribution, leaving the net direction uncertain despite the empirical and documentation gains.
